baseline_fields.evidence_summary: PCEF convergence now includes portable agent state, real repository process-death recovery, bounded A2A HTTP+JSON self-interoperability, and a PCEF-governed repository/CI container-isolation capability. The accepted isolation canary verified observed read-only root and input mounts, blocked input writes, strict tmpfs flags, loopback-only network interfaces, blocked outbound TCP, non-root identity, zero effective Linux capabilities, NoNewPrivs=1, exact PID/RAM/CPU cgroup limits, host-secret non-exposure, and an 8-receipt verified PCEF terminal chain. Production-wide sandbox adoption, VM/microVM equivalence, native device-local sandbox binding, third-party image provenance and external-provider isolation remain unproven.
baseline_fields.single_extra_feature: Sovereign Proof-Carrying Autonomy: consequential execution must prove its authority and observed isolation/effect boundary before PCEF permits terminal completion.
baseline_fields.8x8_parity_gate: Bind every risky production execution lane to an observed isolation receipt, add stronger VM/microVM boundaries where warranted, and retain PCEF as the sole completion law while native and external-provider evidence remain fail-closed.

frontier_patch.definition: Every consequential agent/tool/external effect must carry authorization-bound, idempotent, replay-verifiable proof before terminal completion; risky code execution must additionally prove the observed isolation boundary rather than merely request sandbox flags; a future privacy-preserving attestation layer may prove policy compliance without disclosing prompts, secrets or private topology.
frontier_patch.why_it_is_one_feature: It remains one proof-carrying completion law: authority, execution boundary, effect, verification and terminal state are all evidence-bearing phases rather than unrelated product features.
